post.instagram_caption:
In 1947, engineers found a real moth stuck inside a computer.

It was jammed in a relay of Harvard's Mark II. The team taped it into the logbook with the note "First actual case of bug being found." The page now sits in the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History.

The twist: they didn't invent the word. Thomas Edison was already calling machine faults "bugs" in 1878, which is why the note is a joke.

The lesson: the moth didn't name the bug, it just made it famous.

Source: Smithsonian National Museum of American History, checked Nov 5, 2026.
